The review of PR #2549 found 9 issues. The first two can make the trail report "clean" when it shouldn't be, so I'd fix those before merging.

**Correctness (fix before merge)**
1. **Streamed text runs together** (`review/dump.go:193`). `joinAssistantText` only puts a newline between two text events if one of them isn't a delta. So separate Pi messages, or a retry attempt's partial output, get glued together with no break. A verdict like `request changes` then no longer starts a line, `proseReportsFindings` misses it, and an empty comments array gets treated as clean.
2. **Labeled verdicts are no longer recognized** (`review/trail_report.go:167`). `proseReportsFindings` only checks for bare prefixes. Text like `**Verdict:** request changes`, `Nits:`, `Issues:` or `[p1]` followed by `"comments":[]` is now treated as clean. This undoes the fix in e2df2bb5d (`startsWithFeedbackLabel`).
3. **One blank comment discards all of them** (`trail_report.go:148`). If any comment has an empty body, `decodeTrailComments` rejects the whole array. The code then falls back to prose that has already had the JSON removed, so valid findings are lost. If the judge also wrote no prose, the raw JSON gets posted as the finding instead. The old code just skipped blank comments.
4. **The judge's empty result gets overridden** (`trail_report.go:92`). When the judge returns zero comments, every high-severity reviewer comment is posted anyway, with no dedup. So a false positive the judge dropped still gets posted, and two reviewers flagging the same thing posts it twice. If the judge returns a single low comment instead, all the highs are dropped, so the two cases behave inconsistently.
5. **JSON is stripped when it isn't the contract** (`cmd.go:1644`). `combinedReviewNarratives` removes a trailing JSON object even when it isn't valid contract JSON (ok=false). `stripTrailJSON` doesn't do that, so a reviewer's evidence snippet (say, a `package.json` object) disappears from the trail post but still shows in the local dump.

**Efficiency and design**
6. **Findings reach the judge twice** (`synthesis_prompt.go:67`). The judge prompt includes each reviewer's full narrative, JSON contract line included, so every finding appears both as a bullet and as JSON. Applying `stripTrailJSON` here, as `dump.go` already does, fixes it.
7. **Pi-specific fix in shared code** (`agent/pi/reviewer.go:90`). The shared `Delta` flag works around a Pi-only problem. The Pi parser could instead collect deltas per message and emit one block at `message_end`. That keeps message boundaries, which also fixes #1. The TUI (`tui_detail.go`, `tui_model.go`) still renders each delta as its own block.
8. **Duplicated rules** (`trail_report.go:183`). `isListItem` and `isHighTrailSeverity` repeat what `topLevelBulletText` and `normalizeReviewTrailSeverity` in `review_bridge.go` already do, and they've already drifted: the new ones don't handle `nit`/`p3` or strip punctuation.
9. **Internal wording in user output** (`cmd.go:1609`). Users see `Nothing to report (reviewer JSON: 0 comments from 1 reviewer(s))`. A plain "no findings" line would do.

I haven't checked these by hand or run tests. They're the reviewer's analysis of the source. I also didn't check the diff against your Review Lessons files.

**Proposed lesson** for `Review Lessons/cli.md` (I'll add it only if you approve):
- "When rewriting a parser or classifier, keep the earlier fixes' regression cases (for example, feedback labels like `Nits:`) as tests for the new implementation; a rewrite can silently drop handling that only those cases cover."

Do you want me to fix #1 through #6 on this branch? If so, I'll write a short plan first.
verify the findings and then we decide what to fix

I checked all 9 findings against the code at the PR head (5741eb83b). Seven hold up: four are real bugs (#1, #2, #3, #6) and three are smaller design or cleanup points (#7, #8, #9). The other two (#4, #5) describe behavior the code comments say was chosen deliberately, so they're your call rather than bugs. I tested #1, #2, #3 and #5 by running copies of the functions in the scratchpad against the reported inputs, so no repo files changed. The rest I checked by reading the source.

| # | Finding | Verdict | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Streamed text from separate messages runs together | **Confirmed, and new in this PR** | Two message streams separated by a tool call joined as `"I'll read the diff.request changes — …"`. The prose check then returned false, so the empty comments array was accepted as clean. On `main` each delta got its own line, so the clean check never had this problem. |
| 2 | Labeled verdicts are treated as clean | **Confirmed** | `proseReportsFindings` returned false for `**Verdict:** request changes — …`, `Nits: rename x`, `Issues: …` and `[p1] …`. `findings.go` (added in e2df2bb5d) was deleted by 5741eb83b, so the label handling is gone. Lower impact now: it only matters when a model writes findings in prose but returns an empty comments array, which is exactly the case this check exists for. |
| 3 | One blank comment loses all of them | **Confirmed** | Prose `approve` plus JSON with one real high comment and one blank-body comment gave `ok=false`, 0 comments, prose `"approve"`. The fallback then posts a generic "approve" verdict and the real finding is gone. `main` skipped blank entries instead. |
| 4 | Judge's empty result is overridden by reviewer highs | **Deliberate, but has a real gap** | The comment at `trail_report.go:84` says this is on purpose: an empty judge result can't erase a reviewer's high-severity finding. Two parts are still real: there's no dedup, so two reviewers flagging the same thing post it twice; and if the judge returns even one low comment, every reviewer high is dropped. That inconsistency is the part worth deciding on. |
| 5 | JSON is stripped when it isn't the contract | **Deliberate, low impact** | Reproduced: `splitTrailJSON` removes non-contract JSON from the posted prose, while `stripTrailJSON` keeps it for the local dump. The doc comment says this is on purpose, so malformed contract JSON is never posted as finding text. Losing a quoted config snippet is the cost of that choice. |
| 6 | Reviewer JSON sent to the judge twice | **Confirmed, and new in this PR** | `synthesis_prompt.go:67` uses `joinAssistantText` without `stripTrailJSON`. This PR is what adds the JSON line to reviewer output (`prompt.go`), so the judge now sees each finding twice, plus an example of the output format inside data it's told to treat as untrusted. One-line fix. `manifest.go:684` also stores the JSON line in the narrative; the reviewer didn't flag that, and it matters less. |
| 7 | Pi-only fix put in shared code | **Valid design point** | Accumulating text per message in the Pi parser and emitting it once at `message_end` would fix #1 without the shared `Delta` flag. The reviewer's claim about the TUI is wrong, though: the TUI already showed one block per delta on `main`, so that isn't a regression. |
| 8 | Duplicated bullet and severity rules | **Valid, minor** | The drift is real: `isHighTrailSeverity` strips only `[]`, while `normalizeReviewTrailSeverity` strips `[](){}:*_`. Fixing it isn't simple reuse, though: `review` can't import `cli`, so the normalizer would have to move into `review`. |
| 9 | Internal wording in user output | **Confirmed, cosmetic** | `cmd.go:1609` prints `Nothing to report (reviewer JSON: 0 comments from N reviewer(s))`. |

**My recommendation:**
- **Fix:** #1 (ideally the #7 way, in the Pi parser), #3 (skip blank entries like `main` did), #6 (one line), and #2 (restore the label and verdict-prefix checks, with the e2df2bb5d cases as tests).
- **Decide:** #4. The simplest consistent rule is "dedup reviewer highs, and add them whenever the judge didn't already report them," or else drop the override and trust the judge.
- **Leave or tidy:** #5, #8, #9.

Which of these do you want fixed?
but it does have some out of scope things right?

Trail: https://entire.io/gh/MuskanPaliwal/cli/trails/12

When a reviewer approves a change with nothing to report, `entire review` posts that approval to the Trail as a finding. The Trail then shows an "Unspecified finding" for a review that found nothing.

`reviewTrailFindingInputs` looks for structured comments or Markdown finding bullets in the reviewer output. A clean approval such as

```text
approve - no actionable findings
```

has neither, so the fallback posts the whole output as one severity-less, whole-change comment.

This originally surfaced alongside a Claude stream parsing bug that made Codex the only successful reviewer. #2699 has since fixed the parser. The clean-verdict behavior is independent of it and still reproduces with any reviewer that returns a plain approval.

## What changed

`maybePostReviewToTrail` now skips posting when the review is clean and prints the existing "Nothing to report" notice instead. The check runs before the reviewer outputs are joined:

- With a synthesized verdict, that verdict must be clean.
- Without one (single reviewer, or synthesis produced nothing), every reviewer's output must be clean on its own. One approving reviewer cannot hide another reviewer's findings.

Output is clean when its last non-empty line is an unqualified `approve` and no line is a non-clean verdict. Prompts put the verdict first, so a trailing "Approve once that is fixed." cannot override an earlier `request changes`.

Accepted as clean:

- plain approvals: `approve`, `APPROVE.`, `Approved.`
- Markdown emphasis or headings: `**approve** - ...`, `## approve`
- an approve whose reason says nothing needs fixing: `approve - no actionable defects found.`, `approve with nothing to report`, `approve! looks good.`
- reasoning or chatter before the final verdict line, as long as it cites no file:line

Still posted:

- `request changes`, anywhere in the output
- approvals carrying feedback or a condition: `approve with nits`, `approve with notes`, `approve (nits: ...)`, `approve, but ...`, `approve once ...`, `approved pending ...`, `looks good, though ...`
- any other approve reason, since it may be feedback: `approve - rename x for clarity`, `approve - no tests cover the retry path`
- any finding-shaped line, at any indentation: a bullet, a numbered item, or a severity marker such as `[high]`
- any line containing a file:line pointer such as `retry.go:42`, including the approve reason itself
- labelled or bulleted verdicts the parser does not recognize: `Verdict: approve`, `- approve`
- prose after the verdict line
- a reviewer whose output has no verdict line

When unsure, it posts. A false "clean" would hide a real finding, while a false "not clean" only restores the previous behavior.

`reviewTrailFindingInputs` is unchanged. Its existing test now uses a `request changes` input, since a clean approval no longer reaches it.

## Tests

In `review/posttrail_test.go`, using real single- and multi-reviewer run summaries:

- `TestMaybePostReviewToTrailSkipsCleanVerdicts`: clean synthesized verdicts, a reviewer with preamble before the verdict, and two clean reviewers (one with its own `## Summary` heading) are not posted.
- `TestMaybePostReviewToTrailPostsNonCleanVerdicts`: the non-clean forms above, including approve reasons that carry feedback, plus one reviewer requesting changes or giving no verdict while another approves, are posted.

## Scope

This does not change review prompts, reviewer failure policy, synthesis, Trail API types, or server rendering.

content.text:
Yes. The biggest issue is that the PR has grown well past what its title and description promise. The description still says:

> This does not change review prompts, reviewer failure policy, synthesis, Trail API types, or server rendering.
> `reviewTrailFindingInputs` is unchanged.

Both statements were true of the early commits. The last commit (5741eb83b) replaced the approach: instead of reading the verdict prose, the review now reads a JSON block that reviewers and the judge are asked to append. That commit changes exactly the things the description rules out. The description also still documents the old approve-line rules and test names (`TestMaybePostReviewToTrailSkipsCleanVerdicts`).

Here's how the diff splits up.

**Required by the JSON-block approach** (in scope if you keep that approach, but the description has to say so):
- Reviewer and judge prompt changes (`prompt.go`, `synthesis_prompt.go`), plus the `TrailFindingsJSON` setting passed through `RunConfig`, `SynthesisSink` and `cmd.go`.
- `trail_report.go` and the `review_bridge.go` rewrite.
- Hiding the JSON block wherever output is shown (`dump.go`, `fix.go`, `synthesis_sink.go`). Otherwise every user would see the raw JSON.
- The Pi `Delta` flag. On `main` each streamed Pi fragment is joined with a newline, so a JSON line split mid-string would fail to parse. It's needed, but it changes how Pi text is joined in every mode, not just trail mode. That's why #1 belongs to this PR, and why I'd move the fix into the Pi parser (#7) rather than shared types.

**Beyond the stated goal ("don't post clean verdicts"):**
1. **Judge override (#4).** Reposting reviewer high-severity comments when the judge returns none is a new rule about how much to trust the judge, unrelated to clean verdicts. It's also the source of the duplicate-posting finding. I'd drop it, or make it its own PR.
2. **Structured findings without a judge.** Single-reviewer and no-judge runs now post native findings with severity and location from each reviewer's JSON, merged together. That's a feature upgrade: before, only the judge's last line was parsed as JSON. It's reasonable, but it's new behavior to describe or split out.
3. **`synthesisPromptOptions` refactor.** This one is fine. It's mechanical and needed for the new parameter.
4. **Branch name.** `fix-claude-review-stream-parser` comes from the parser bug that #2699 has since fixed. That's cosmetic, but reviewers may find it confusing.

**My recommendation:** keep the JSON-block approach. The five earlier commits were a series of special-case fixes to prose parsing, and the JSON block is the more robust fix. But:
- drop the judge override (#4);
- fix #1 inside the Pi parser instead of with the shared flag (#7);
- fix #2, #3 and #6;
- rewrite the title and description for what the PR actually does now, e.g. "fix(review): read trail findings from a JSON block instead of parsing verdict prose", including the prompt changes.

The alternative is to go back to f6d5376d2 or earlier for a smaller prose-only fix and open the JSON block as a follow-up PR. That's less to review, but it brings back the fragile prose parsing.

Which way do you want to go? If it's the first, I'll write the change plan and the new PR description for you to approve before I edit anything.

# General Review Lessons

- Make a guard's zero-match check count only the matches it is meant to protect. Matches that are always present, like the guard's own allowed cases, keep the check from ever firing.
- Test a guard by planting a violation and by breaking its detection, and see it fail both times. A guard that passes on clean code proves nothing.
- Before acting on a review finding, check whether existing tests or contracts explain the current shape. A structural test can be why the code looks the way it does.
- When code reads a user-owned config into a typed struct and writes it back, keep the fields it does not model. Any new reason to rewrite the file otherwise silently deletes user data.
- Make a new outer timeout longer than every internal budget on that path. Otherwise the kill fires before the code's own graceful fallback.
- Before setting an explicit timeout, look up the platform's current default for that exact event; an explicit value can shorten the budget rather than add one.
- When splitting known from unknown JSON keys to preserve them, decode only the exact known keys and keep every other key, case variants included, as unknown. `encoding/json` matches field names case-insensitively, so decoding the whole object lets a key like `"Command"` overwrite the real field.
- When a change makes a fix command riskier or changes which command to run, update every place that tells the user to run it (status, doctor, help text). Otherwise one screen sends people to the safe fix and the next to the destructive one.
# cli Review Lessons

- A capability guard must catch every way to reach a capability, including anonymous and local interfaces, not only the named interface. Go interfaces are structural, so a type assertion to any interface with the same method skips the `As*` gate.
- If `InstallHooks` can rewrite an agent's config without adding hooks, report it through `StaleHookReporter`. `count == 0` alone prints "already installed", which hides the rewrite.
- When a change alters what Entire writes into an agent's config, make it reach existing installs, not only new ones: users rarely re-run `entire enable`. Add an `entire doctor` repair for anything safe to fix silently, and check that doctor does not report the old config as OK.

The agreed fixes are in, and `mise run check` passes: format and lint are clean, unit and integration tests pass, and the Vogon (53/53) and roger-roger (4/4) canaries pass. Nothing is committed yet.

**What changed** (10 files, +203 / −116)
- **#1:** The Pi parser now sets `Delta` only on a fragment that continues the current message. It resets at `message_end` and `auto_retry_start`, so separate messages and retries start on a new line again. `joinAssistantText` adds a newline before every non-continuation event.
- **#2:** `proseReportsFindings` handles `Verdict:` labels again, plus `Nits:` / `Issues:` / `Concerns:` / `Suggestions:` and the full set of severity markers (`[p1]`, `P2:`, `high —`, …).
- **#3:** Comments with a blank body are skipped instead of invalidating the whole array.
- **#4:** The judge override is removed, along with `isHighTrailSeverity`. When a judge runs, its JSON alone decides what's posted.
- **#6:** The judge prompt now leaves out the reviewers' JSON lines.
- **#9:** The notice is always the plain "Nothing to report" line.
- The docs section in `review-command.md` is updated to match.

**Tests:** I wrote the new and changed tests first and confirmed they failed against the old code (8 label cases, blank body, judge override, notice wording, judge prompt, Pi boundaries). They all pass now.

**Differences from the plan:**
- For #9, I dropped the reason entirely instead of sending it to `logging.Debug`. Without the override, the only reason left for skipping is "no comments", so a log line wouldn't tell anyone anything.
- One case I noticed while writing it: a clean line that happens to start with a marker followed by a delimiter, like `Low - risk change.`, now posts. That fits the PR's rule of posting when unsure.

**Not verified:** a real `entire review` run in trail mode against a live trail. That needs paid agent calls, so I didn't run one.

**Commit message for your approval:**

```
fix(review): tighten the trail JSON contract checks

Keep streamed Pi text from different messages or retry attempts on
separate lines, so a verdict after a tool call still starts its own
line and the clean-review check sees it.

Treat labeled verdicts, feedback labels such as "Nits:", and priority
markers such as "[p1]" as findings when the comments array is empty.

Skip comments with a blank body instead of rejecting the whole array.

Let the judge's comments alone decide what is posted, drop reviewer
JSON lines from the judge prompt, and keep the "Nothing to report"
notice free of internal wording.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
```

**Rewritten PR description for your approval.** The current one describes the old prose-parsing approach.

> Trail: https://entire.io/gh/MuskanPaliwal/cli/trails/12
>
> When a review finds nothing, `entire review` in trail mode still posts the approval to the Trail as an "Unspecified finding".
>
> The poster had no structured way to tell a clean review from one with findings, so it fell back to posting the whole verdict as one whole-change comment. Earlier commits on this branch tried to recognize clean verdicts from prose, and each new phrasing needed another rule. This PR replaces that with an explicit output contract.
>
> ## What changed
>
> In trail mode only, reviewers and the judge end their output with one JSON line:
>
> ```json
> {"summary":"...","comments":[{"severity":"high","body":"...","location":{...}}]}
> ```
>
> The instruction comes last in the prompt, after profile and per-run text. It is not added for a verbatim `prompt` override. Posting reads this line:
>
> - `"comments":[]` posts nothing and prints "Nothing to report", unless the prose contradicts it with a list item, a severity marker (`[high]`, `[p1]`, `P2:`), a feedback label (`Nits:`, `Issues:`), or a `request changes` / `approve with nits` verdict (also when labeled `Verdict:`). In that case the prose is posted.
> - Comments post as native findings with their severity and location. Entries without a body are skipped.
> - When a judge runs, its line alone decides what is posted. Without a judge, each reviewer's line is read and the comments are merged.
> - A missing or malformed line posts the prose, with any trailing JSON removed, split into findings by top-level bullet. When unsure, it posts.
>
> The JSON line is hidden wherever results are shown (live output, `entire review` detail, the judge's input) and kept in the saved manifest.
>
> Pi streams text as fragments. On `main` every fragment became its own line, which would split the JSON line. Fragments of one message now join without a separator, and each new message or retry attempt starts a new line.
>
> ## Scope
>
> This changes the reviewer and judge prompts in trail mode only. Local output, reviewer failure policy, Trail API types, and server rendering are unchanged.
>
> ## Tests
>
> - `review/trail_report_test.go`: clean and non-clean judge and reviewer outputs, fenced and pretty-printed JSON, malformed contracts, labeled verdicts and feedback labels, blank-body comments, a judge `[]` alongside a reviewer finding, and streamed fragments across messages.
> - `agent/pi/reviewer_test.go`: fragment continuation resets at each message and retry.
> - `review/synthesis_prompt_test.go`: the trail-mode judge prompt ends with the contract, and reviewer JSON is not repeated in the judge's input.
